text:
The macro backdrop continues to firm in ways we think matter more than the headlines suggest. Inflation has settled to 2.4%, the policy rate sits at 4.50%, and high yield spreads have compressed to 320bps — a level that, not so long ago, would have been read as an all-clear signal. Equities extended their gains this quarter, and perhaps more consequentially for our world, new issuance windows have reopened across the credit markets. For a vintage that has spent the better part of a year absorbing the cost of carry, this is the kind of tape that lets operators get back to operating rather than refinancing.

Against that backdrop, the portfolio delivered a reported return of +3.2% for the quarter, bringing year-to-date performance to +6.0% and since-inception returns to +45.0%. Public equities were up +4.0% over the same period — a modest differential that we view less as a gap to explain and more as evidence that our marks continue to reflect the underlying discipline of the businesses we own, not the daily sentiment of public markets. NAV index stands at 106.0, a figure our valuation committee continues to stand behind. We do not chase index correlation for its own sake; we chase cash flow durability, and that has been the story of this book since inception.

The financing-cost pressure that shaped our tone last quarter has not disappeared, but it has moved from acute to what we'd characterize as a temporary dislocation working itself out in real time — helped considerably by the reopening of issuance windows. Portfolio companies that were bridging on expensive paper are finding a friendlier market to term out into, and our operating teams have used the interim period to drive margin rather than wait for markets to bail them out. That is, frankly, the quieter half of this story: the leverage was never going to fix itself, so we fixed the businesses instead.

Looking ahead, we remain constructive but not complacent. Spread compression and reopened issuance are constructive tailwinds, and should conditions continue to normalize, we believe recovery in exit activity could unfold over coming quarters. That said, we are watching the durability of this rally carefully — issuance windows can shut as quickly as they open, and a prudent GP treats a good quarter as an opportunity to term out risk, not declare victory. Our conversations with long-term partners reflect the same measured optimism: constructive on direction, disciplined on timing.

Onward.
